title: Focus neighbors "next" and "previous" don't properly jump over hidden controls in some edge cases.
body:
### Tested versions

Tested in 4.4.1.stable, 4.5.stable, 4.5.1.rc2

### System information

Godot v4.5.stable - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6094) - AMD Ryzen 5 7600X 6-Core Processor (12 threads) - 31.10 GiB memory

### Issue description

"Next" and "Previous" focus neighbors do not jump over hidden nodes when controls are not children of other controls. The directional ones work just fine jumping over, which is why this can be seen as an issue.

This is what I mean by "jumping": lets say the "Down" focus neighbor chain is manually set to go through three buttons: 
      B1 -> B2 -> B3 -> B1
If B2 becomes hidden, then the "Down" focus chain should jump over B2 and automatically become:
      B1 -> B3 -> B1
Which works as intended.

The same is not true for "Next" and "Previous" focus chains--which is why I consider this an issue and not a feature request.

Not being children of controls is important in seeing this since controls already automatically set focus neighbors of their children that make the most sense position-wise when one is hidden. 
I haven't tested, but I would assume that, even with parent controls, similar issues appear if you set the focus chains in unintuitive ways that cannot be predicted by parent controls when one becomes hidden.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set at least three control (like buttons) as a child of a Node2D. Predictably, this breaks the automatic focus neighbor assign.
2. Assign focus neighbor "next" and "previous". The focus now moves with tab and shift-tab as predicted.
3. Hide one of the neighbors in the middle of the focus chain, and rerun. Now tab/ shift-tab will not skip over the hidden neighbor. Compare behavior to focus neighbor "up" and "down", or "left" and "right", which works correctly by jumping over.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A - setup takes seconds. If really needed, I can provide.
